unit_text: On Thursday I reread Lena's email about the ethics complaint
copied one sentence from the draft incident log into the reply to Omar before the meeting with Priya
my manager.
I kept wondering whether she had forwarded the thread to shield me, to warn Omar, or to leave a record in case I quit
my jaw tightened when the email itself only said, "we should talk before noon."
During the meeting with Priya
my manager
I admitted I still hadn't sent the corrected invoice to the clinic
apologized for freezing during Tuesday's intake interview.
Afterward I opened the unsent reply to Lena
deleted one paragraph
restored it
kept hearing Tessa laugh from the scene in the novel where the sister breaks the cup.
I couldn't tell whether I was angry at Tessa, at the novel, or at the part of me that keeps treating every sentence like a verdict.
The rest of the evening was me arguing with my own project memo.
I wrote "clarity is a promise we make to strangers" in the margin
crossed it out
rewrote the last line
compared the risk table to last night's trace
circled the row about the rollback window.
I still didn't know whether the bug belonged in the cache, in the queue, in the parser, or in my assumptions.
At dinner with my brother Arun he asked whether the scan had scared me again.
I told him I was okay
I wasn't.
I felt ashamed, furious, relieved, and unexpectedly lonely all at once
I could barely swallow.
Before sleep I listened to the voicemail from Dr. Imani
did not call back
kept telling myself I already knew what it said.
I don't.
Part of me wanted the call to be about the scan, and part of me wanted it to be about nothing medical at all.
I missed Maya
I did not text her.
If I call back, it will be about the scan
if I don't, it will still be about the scan.
